newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen stabilising next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen stabilising next week.

text.p: The Polish bourse is likely to stabilise next week as the general horizontal trend continues in the run-up to parliamentary elections on September 21, analysts said.

Analysts were divided on whether slight growth or falls were more likely next week, with some seeing a light uptrend as profits taken from large newcomers Bank Handlowy and copper firm KGHM would flow to other stocks.

"The market needs money to go up and that money is going to go via Handlowy and KGHM and in an indirect way to other firms," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.

Other analysts said concerns over the current flooding in the industrial south as well as the election run-up would dampen buying and cause falls next week. Thousands of square kilometres in southern Poland lie under water despite a halt after five days of downpours.
Analysts said firms in the waters' path could be exposed to selling pressure, although southern-based construction firms could benefit once the region dried out.
Late this week the bourse suspended trade in industrial boilermaker Rafako and electrode maker ZEW for an indefinite period as the floodwaters rose in the town of Raciborz.
Analysts said insurance firms should also fall financial victim to the floods, including large state-owned PZU, whose partial sale is seen possible by the end of the month.

"It (insurance claims) could be painful for the bourse -- PZU invests in a lot of listed firms and I think they might get rid of some shares to pay," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at WBK AIB Asset Management.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.7 percent this week to 15,832.8 points.

Analysts said macroeconomic signals were mixed despite forecasts of Poland maintaining 5.5 percent economic growth in the coming years and its successful fight with inflation, seen at around 14.6 percent year-on-year in June.
On Tuesday the central bank said it might need to increase market rates further to control its operational target of reserve money growth.

Analysts said Handlowy, up 0.5 percent on the week, and KGHM, up 2.1 percent on Friday after starting trade 11.9 percent above its 21-zloty institutional investor price on Thursday, should continue to stabilise next week as large investors finished accumulating the large-cap stocks.
